findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the heat dish machine is still not repaired, and not reaching a high enough temperatures for sanitizing (165°F). PIC is working with a repair service to get the heat machine back up to a sanitizing temperature of 165°F. Facility is using their triple sinks to sanitize until the heat dish machine is repaired. Inspector will follow up with facility to confirm machine is repaired. Ensure that the temperature of a heat dish machine shall reach 165°F.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the heat dish machine was not reaching a high enough temperatures for sanitizing, with the highest temperature reached after 3 cycles being 141.8°F. PIC will contact a repair service to get the heat machine back up to a sanitizing temperature of 165°F. Facility will use their triple sinks to sanitize until the heat dish machine is repaired. Inspector will follow up with facility to confirm machine is repaired. Ensure that the temperature of a heat dish machine shall reach 165°F.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a container of cream (a TCS product) with a date mark beyond the 7 day rule. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the cream, and discussed with Inspector rules for date marking TCS, RTE products. Ensure that any TCS, RTE foods are date marked if they will be in the facility beyond 24 hours of their open or prep date, with the date of prep or open being day 1, and day 7 being the day of final use or discard.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: 2ND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of dust on the walk-in freezer fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in freezer fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed 2 employee bathrooms that are used by women where there was not a lid on the trash receptacles. Inspector discussed with PIC the importance of providing a lidded trash receptacles for bathrooms used by women, including for hygiene purposes and to protect the facility’s plumbing from improperly discarded feminine hygiene products. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have a covered trash receptacle.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a wet mop being stored in the lower basin of a mop bucket where it cannot air-dry. Observed 2 wet mops being stored against a wall (which can soil the wall), with one of two mops not being inverted and allowed to air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC relocated both mops to better locations where they can air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Ensure mops be stored in positions and locations where they can fully air-dry between uses.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed various white powders (ex. sugar, flour, salt) in the kitchen that had been removed from the original packaging and moved into large containers but were not labeled. All easily mistakable foods not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that any white powder re-packaged into storage containers are labeled with the common name of the food by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed a large container of cream filling stored with the scoop handle directly touching the filling. The PIC was informed and they removed the scoop from the container. They stated that the company policy is that scoops should not be stored within food containers. The PIC will be educating employees about the proper procedure. Ensure that scoop handles for ready-to-eat foods are always stored above food to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the cove base underneath the front triple sink is not attached to the wall. The cove base must be sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the cove base is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed the facility was preparing donuts during the inspection but there was not a sanitizer bucket available. The PIC was informed and they made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of dust on the walk-in freezer fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in freezer fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTIONS DATED 08/23/2022 and 12/14/2023.

Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on a donut prep counter during the inspection. In-use wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses. Wiping cloths can never be stored on counters once wet. The wiping cloth was placed in a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always stored in chemical solution between uses and laundered daily. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop holder by the ice machine was soiled with debris on the bottom. The ice scoop holder and ice scoop were removed from service and cleaned during the inspection. After cleaning the ice scoop holder was free of debris. Ensure that the ice scoop holder is cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in freezer fans have an accumulation of dust. The fans must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure the fans are cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION ON 08/23/2022.

The hand sink in the far east room of the building is observed to have scissors, a wet wiping cloth and a soiled spatula in the basin. Hand sinks may not be used for any purposes beside hand washing including but not limited to dumping, cleaning or any other activity. Ensure that hand sinks are properly stocked and accessible at all times and not used for any other purpose. Inspector will return on 12/18/2023 to ensure hand sinks are stocked, accessible and only used for hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 08/23/2022.

Inspector observed multiple wet wiping cloths sitting in the far east room of the facility. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses and not allowed to be sitting out. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored properly at all times. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 08/29/2022. 

The ware washing room of the facility has several areas of missing/peeling base coving, exposed raw wood which is molding, pits in the floor which are accumulating water, and sections of wall that are deteriorating along the bottom. This area is subject to large amounts of food/water spray. All surfaces must be repaired/replaced to be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that these surface meet the requirements of the 2017 FDA Food Code as adopted by being smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The basement of the facility is observed to be heavily soiled following repair of leaking waste water from damaged plumbing. Cleaning must occur to remove residue from draining waste water. Clean the basement: use a bleach solution to soak walls and floors. 
Ensure that the basement remains clean and dry in the future. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Complete repairs in the wash room of the facility including replacement/sealing of floors, replacement/repair of window/fan unit, sealing of ware washing equipment to walls. Make sure that the room is constructed in a way that floors, walls and ceiling are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The bathroom at the back food prep area next to the mop sink is not being used at this time per owner. The bathroom is not stocked with hand soap or paper towels. However, there is hand washing signage. Any hand sink designated a hand washing sink with such signage must be available and properly stocked for hand washing at all times. Signage has been removed during inspection. Corrected on site. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Several drain flies were observed around the window/fan of the dish washing room and throughout the facility. Owner states that the windows/fan unit are anticipated to be replaced. Orkin is in charge of pest control on a monthly basis or more often as needed. Ensure that the facility is free of flies and other pests. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several wiping cloths throughout the facility including used as a grease catch under the fryers, used to plug a hole in the floor, used for wiping water from the frosting machine, and in several other discrete areas throughout the establishment. Dry wiping cloths may be used. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution if being used on surfaces and equipment. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored appropriately and not scattered throughout the facility. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A tray rack next to the fryers was observed to have several in-use utensils stored on top of moderately soiled racks and on top of a used cloth glove. In use utensils may only be resting on cleaned and sanitized surfaces. Tongs should be hung to prevent contact of food surface with other materials and equipment. Do not store utensils on top of gloves or other absorbent surfaces.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single use forks and knives on the service line were observed to be facing multiple directions. These single use items must be stored in a direction which facilities grabbing the handle without touching the eating surface of others. Ensure that all single use utensils are facing the same direction in their respective containers. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a cloth glove on the rack to the right of the fryer being used to rest utensils on. Cloth gloves must not be in direct contact with food contact surfaces. Remove the cloth glove from the area and use it only for designated purposes. 

Observed a used, soiled plastic glove sitting on the countertop where food preparation was occurring. When used gloves are removed, they must be discarded to prevent contamination. 

3-304.15: (B) Slash-resistant gloves used to protect hands shall be used with FOOD that is subsequently cooked. (C) Slash-resistant gloves may be used with RTE FOOD if gloves are SMOOTH, durable, and nonabsorbent, or if gloves are covered with SMOOTH, durable, nonabsorbent gloves. (D) Cloth gloves may not be used with direct contact with FOOD unless FOOD is cooked.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
There is an old butcher block counter top at the rear of the kitchen with large groves. If being retained, the surface of the counter top must be sealed and resurfaced so that it is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

4-501.12: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and SANITIZED, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Overall, the facility is in need of deep cleaning. The general areas of the facility are adequately cleaned and there is no accumulation of debris and residue. However, the rest of the facility has been neglected. There is a significant amount of debris and residue around edges of the floor underneath equipment in all areas of the facility. Shelving units throughout the facility are soiled and there is oil dripping from them. Ledges throughout the facility are observed to be soiled. Ventilation units throughout the facility are soiled. Wiring underneath the fryer has a significant amount of grease buildup. Ensure that these areas are cleaned by the next inspection.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be leaking from the plumbing system in the facility into the basement resulting in standing, stagnant waste water. The large pipe leading directly to the drain pipe is leaking significantly. Repair the plumbing system. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
A water pipe in the basement and the foundation itself is in disrepair resulting in sewage leaking into the basement. Repair the system and foundation to allow for sewage to be properly conveyed to the sanitary sewer system. Pictures have been sent to owner and CK to forward to a plumber. Inspector spoke with CK who advised to have the follow-up in two weeks instead of three days due to availability of repairs and to refer to City of Springfield. The problem will be referred to the city plumber for review and a follow-up will occur in two weeks. 

5-402.13: SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Trim throughout the facility is observed to be missing or damaged. There must be an easily cleanable intersection between floor and wall in all areas subject to moisture. Caulking around the mop sink is damaged and/or missing and must be replaced. The faucet of the hand sink in the bathroom next to the mop sink is coming apart and must be repaired. The exhaust hood above the fryers appears to have draining grease coming from it and there was smoke from the fryers present throughout the facility over the course of the inspection. Have the exhaust hood inspected and repaired if recommended. Flooring throughout the facility is cracked and in disrepair. Repair any cracked tiles. Trim around doorways is in disrepair and in need of maintenance. Wood trim must be sealed unless it cannot be sealed and easily cleanable at which point the trim must be replaced. The countertop to the right of the back storage area has a corner which is heavily damaged. Replace this countertop. Overall, the facility must have smooth and easily cleanable surfaces in any location where food preparation is occurring. Ensure that all these surfaces are in good repair at the time of next inspection. The walk in freezer and proofed had seals which are in need of repair. Ensure that these seals are repaired or replaced to allow the seal to function effectively. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no CFPM present during inspection. Employee was a food handler. A certified food protection manager must be present during all hours of operation. This is a repeat violation from the pre-opening on 10/01/19.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to turn off faucet without a barrier. Ensure a barrier is used when hand washing and turning off faucets. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

Observed no soap in the bathroom near the mop sink. Discussed proper stocking of soap at all hand sinks with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed a hole in the porcelain of the hand sink near the mop area. Repair hand sink by next routine inspection so it is smooth.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following surfaces in need of repair:
1. Frontline: a) ceiling tiles are acoustic (should be smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable)
2. Bathroom frontline: a) replace ceiling tiles in both bathrooms
3. Office/triple sink: a) ceiling tiles over the triple sink and hand sink should be smooth, easily cleanable
B) repair threshold from frontline to office/smooth transition
4. Dish room: a) seal wall left when entering room (look low, where coving is missing/wall damaged)
B) scrape and repaint plumbing lines
C) replace missing baseboard around sanitizing sink and rinse sink
D) smooth out deep groves in the floor that are allowing ponding water

These are repeat violations from the pre-opening on 10/01/19. Next inspector, please refer to these violations on the pre-opening and recheck at next routine inspection.

New violations:
1. Mop room: coving throughout the mop room is needed
2. Walk-in freeze: coving left of the door at the walk-in freezer
3. Room into decorating room (where ovens are): caulk hand sink at this area
4. Decorating room: seal the decorating table (left corner and front seal)

Ensure repairs by next routine inspection on 2022.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Dishroom still needs repaired. PIC stated area will be repaired by 02/20. Bathroom (in main kitchen) will be removed and made into storage. Coving and Trim still need placed in various areas.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: Employees have taken course. More employees will take course. Ref. 750. 540.
